reviewBoundary: Three new complete junior fifteen-gap four-choice narratives: lift outage, collaborative story endings and concert programmes. Fictional cases; same-author contextual/all-alternative review, not independent calibration.

units.title: The lift was out of service
units.alignmentNote: One complete original fifteen-gap four-choice narrative, using source level/family structure only.

materials.title: The lift was out of service
materials.text:
When the lift in our building stopped working, a notice said repairs would take two days. I complained about the ____1____. Then I saw Mrs Bell beside the entrance with two shopping bags. She lived on the sixth floor and was looking ____2____ at the notice.

I offered to carry the bags. One contained eggs, so we moved ____3____. I took that bag. Halfway up, she needed a ____4____. We sat on the landing and talked about the vegetables she had bought.

I had expected to finish quickly and run home. Instead, I learned that the bags were for a supper she shared with two neighbours. One could not leave his flat that day. My little offer was helping more than one ____5____.

The next morning, another student asked why I was waiting by the door. I explained. He offered to help with the ____6____ bag. We asked the manager where to leave a ____7____.

She suggested a short message with the hours we were available. We did not promise to carry everything at any time. A clear ____8____ was better than a generous promise we could not keep.

By evening, the lift was repaired. Our temporary job was ____9____. Mrs Bell brought us two apples, not as payment but as a thank-you. I had first seen the broken lift as an ____10____ to my own day. It had also revealed how differently neighbours used the same building. We did not need to wait for another ____11____ to greet them. Now I knew a few more names and when someone might welcome a ____12____. The stairs had not become shorter, but the building felt less ____13____. No lift repair could ____14____ that familiarity on its own, and I wanted to ____15____ it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: With the lift unavailable, residents climb stairs. Walls, windows and roof are not the walking route.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Six floors with bags makes the repair notice a source of worry. Anger, secrecy and sleepiness are not established.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Fragile eggs require careful carrying. Speed could break them; silence/location outside do not protect the contents.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Stopping on the landing gives her a rest. A ticket, basket and recipe do not explain sitting midway.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The food serves several neighbours, so help reaches more than one person. Shop/floor/egg do not name the beneficiaries.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Sharing the heavier bag is useful help. Empty/invisible bags require no carrying, and price does not define the load.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The manager suggests a short written message, a note. Bags/tools/recipes do not announce availability.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Stated hours create a clear arrangement instead of an unlimited promise. Picture, stairs and uniform do not define the help schedule.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The repaired lift ends the temporary job, so over. Hidden, late and expensive do not mean completed.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The narrator initially resents a disruption to the day. Answer/invitation/advantage do not express that complaint.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Another lift breakdown is not needed for ongoing neighbour contact. Apples/supper/notices are not the mechanical event that prompted help.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Welcome a hand means welcome help. Bills, warnings and complaints are not the positive support described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Knowing names makes the building less anonymous. Its height, age/design and number of occupants do not change.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The repair alone cannot create neighbourly familiarity; the shared help does. Notice, break and carry do not express producing that social connection.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The narrator wants to keep the new familiarity. Sale, forgetting and measurement do not preserve it.

units.title: The dragon was waiting for an ending
units.alignmentNote: One complete original fifteen-gap four-choice narrative, using source level/family structure only.

materials.title: The dragon was waiting for an ending
materials.text:
Our teacher stopped an adventure just as a dragon opened a door. "What happens next?" she asked. We each had five minutes to write an ____1____.

I made the dragon breathe fire and chase everyone away. I thought an exciting story needed the biggest possible ____2____. My friend Hana wrote that the dragon had come to return a borrowed saucepan. Her version made us ____3____.

The teacher asked us to reread the opening. The dragon carried a bag, and smoke came from the chimney behind it. Those details could support more than one ____4____. Nothing had said it was angry.

We read our versions aloud. One student made the dragon a traveller looking for shelter; another made it afraid of a small mouse. The teacher did not choose one official ____5____. Instead, we discussed which details each version used and which it ____6____.

Hana suggested that my chase needed a reason. I added a broken egg outside the dragon's home. Now its anger had a ____7____, not just a loud entrance. She also changed her saucepan story to explain why it was returning so late.

Our endings remained different, but both became ____8____. We had not copied each other. We had helped one another connect an idea with the words already ____9____.

I kept writing. I still liked a fast chase, but I noticed when noise was taking the place of a ____10____. A surprising ending did not have to ignore the beginning. It could make an earlier detail ____11____ in a new way. The club had given us freedom with one ____12____: our choices should make sense. Next week, I brought the saucepan version to read again, with Hana's ____13____. My favourite story was not necessarily my ____14____. Sometimes another person's strange idea opened a door I had not thought to ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The unfinished adventure needs an ending. Address/invitation/advertisement are not its continuation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Fire and a chase create danger, the narrator’s initial excitement strategy. Reward, kitchen and audience do not name that threat.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The unexpected saucepan return is humorous and makes listeners laugh. Sleep, crying and departure are not the reaction described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: A bag and chimney smoke can support different interpretations of the scene. They do not create multiple physical bags/doors/chimneys.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The teacher allows several reasoned continuations rather than an official answer. Dragon/student/minute do not name the chosen solution.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The discussion checks which opening details a version ignores. Printing/borrowing/counting do not express leaving evidence unused.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: A broken egg gives the dragon a cause for anger. Sound, price and colour do not supply that motive.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Adding explanations strengthens both stories without making them identical. No shortening or aging is the improvement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: They connect ideas to the opening words already provided. Forgotten/erased remove that base, and sale is irrelevant.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Noise cannot substitute for a reason that makes action meaningful. The other nouns are story objects/characters, not logical motivation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: An earlier detail can matter differently after a surprising ending. Disappearance, shrinking and breaking are not new significance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The freedom has a condition that choices make sense. A prize, fee and table do not express that requirement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Reading Hana’s version with her permission respects authorship. Saucepan, anger and silence do not authorise sharing it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The narrator likes Hana’s story, so the favourite need not be the narrator’s own. Teacher’s is not at issue; printed/longest compare other features.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Trying a door metaphorically means exploring a possibility. Closing, painting and hiding do not explore a new route.

units.title: The man who kept leaving his seat
units.alignmentNote: One complete original fifteen-gap four-choice narrative, using source level/family structure only.

materials.title: The man who kept leaving his seat
materials.text:
During a school concert, a man near the front left his seat twice. Elena, waiting to play the piano, thought he was ____1____. She disliked someone leaving before her turn.

When he returned carrying a pair of glasses, she looked away. The helper came backstage and began describing how the visitors were connected, then laughed at her complicated ____2____. What mattered was that his companion could not read the small programme print.

He had gone to his car for stronger glasses, then to the desk to ask whether a larger copy was ____3____. Could Elena wait while they helped his companion?

Elena felt her irritation ____4____. She had turned two short departures into a story about somebody's ____5____ in the music. The real explanation had nothing to do with her performance.

She said she could wait. When she finally played, she saw both visitors sitting quietly, the programme open between them. They stayed until the final ____6____.

After the concert, the man thanked the organisers for helping. While helping clear the chairs, Elena asked whether programmes could be printed more ____7____.

The helper suggested offering a few large-print copies at the entrance. It was a small ____8____ that could help overlooked visitors.

Elena still wanted an attentive audience. She had not learned that every interruption must be ____9____. She had learned that its cause might be ____10____ before she understood it. Her view from the piano was important, but not ____11____. People had needs beyond listening to her. Preparing a performance meant considering some of those needs, not merely expecting perfect ____12____. Next time, she checked the programmes before practising. The larger copies did not ____13____ her audience's attention; they made participation easier. Looking out from the stage, she saw fewer signs to ____14____ and more people she hoped to ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Elena initially interprets departures as boredom. Excitement/helpfulness are not her irritated assumption; fame is unrelated.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The helper laughs at an overly complicated explanation of the relationship. Programme is the document, performance the concert and journey travel, not the tangled account.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The visitor asks whether a large-print copy is available to use. Expense, concealment and familiarity are not the request for a usable version.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Learning a non-dismissive reason makes irritation fade. Grow/return/spread would intensify or renew it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: She assumed a lack of interest in music. Confidence, skill and pleasure are not reasons for fearing he had walked out from boredom.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Staying to the final note means hearing the music through. Seat/copy are objects, and minute is time rather than the musical ending emphasised.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Larger readable print makes programmes clearer. Secrecy, speed and lower cost do not directly improve legibility.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Offering larger copies is a practical adjustment. It is not a prize, excuse or musical performance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: She need not welcome every interruption; she should avoid guessing motives. Counted, recorded and priced do not name the emotional acceptance being qualified.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The cause was unknown until the helper explained. Obvious contradicts the mistaken story; unimportant/musical do not state her lack of information.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The pianist’s viewpoint matters but is incomplete. Relevant/personal/valuable do not express the missing other perspectives.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: She had expected perfect audience behaviour without considering needs. Music is the performance, chairs/programmes tools, not the conduct demanded of visitors.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Large print supports rather than demands attention. Hiding/replacing/dividing are not what the programmes were expected to command.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Fewer signs to misread contrasts with earlier false interpretation. Reading/printing/counting are not the interpretive error.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The change is towards welcoming people rather than judging/avoiding/correcting them from the stage.
